content.title: About
content.content: Greek yogurt with no added sugar, enriched with fruit puree (e.g., strawberry, mango, or blueberry). It is made from whole cow's milk, strained to achieve a thick, creamy texture, and contains minimal lactose.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Greek yogurt contains two to three times more protein than regular yogurt.
Straining removes whey, making the product denser and lower in moisture.
Being sugar‑free gives it a lower glycemic index, beneficial for blood‑sugar control.
Fruit puree is often prepared without added sugars or preservatives.
Traditional Greek yogurt is made from whole milk, though low‑fat versions exist.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: A 200 ml serving provides about 15–20 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of probiotics
items.content: Live cultures such as Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: No added sugar helps keep calorie count low and stabilizes blood glucose levels.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Yogurt supplies calcium for bone health and is often fortified with vitamin D.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: When made from whole milk, it retains omega‑3 and omega‑6 fatty acids.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Although some lactose is removed during straining, it may still cause discomfort for highly intolerant individuals.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey should avoid this product.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some brands add a pinch of salt for flavor; check the label if you monitor sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy it straight from the cup, blend into smoothies, use as a base for sauces, dressings, or desserts. The fruit puree makes it a great topping for granola, nuts, and honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the yogurt refrigerated at 2–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may become grainy.
